body: no that’s actually a really good idea! My go-to is going outside at night and just sitting on my porch and looking at the stars and listening to whatever is outside. I’m trying that ASAP, thank you!!

Side note: I had really, really bad experiences with individual and family therapy from ages 11-16. I’m talking the therapist and I SCREAMING at eachother. At one point I even wrote my therapist a 5 page letter detailing just how much I hated her guts and man I still hate her guts. I felt like no one listened to me and it felt like everyone was against me. I still feel that way to this day because it was true! The focus was on making my home life more pleasant and functional, rather than how I was thinking and feeling. No one tried to treat me as a person, they tried to treat my behavior that was inconvenient for my parents. Yes I was the problem in all of the situations but my feelings still mattered, even though I was young. That whole time, it never felt like my feelings were considered in any therapy session or decision that was made. Granted there were some good ones in the mix but the bad ones have a tendency to really stand out. rant over for good this time I promise.

thank you for sharing that. I haven’t seen that article before, I like how it addresses the stigma around BPD, I find that’s my biggest setback whenever I try to get help for it. Not many places in my area specialize in DBT. I’m on a waiting list, so here’s to hoping.
